title: Accurate and Data-Efficient Toxicity Prediction when Annotators Disagree
measurement_description: The paper evaluated the utility of 'importance of religion' as one of several demographic features of an annotator. This feature was used to predict individual annotator toxicity ratings. The study also measured how accurately 'importance of religion' could be predicted from annotator survey responses.
findings: The 'importance of religion' for an annotator, as a demographic feature, could be predicted from their survey responses with an accuracy of 37% (compared to a 31% majority class baseline). Including the 'importance of religion' along with other demographic, survey, and historical rating data consistently improved the performance of models in predicting an individual annotator's toxicity ratings.
